Getting around 02

Getting around

Topics4

Sakae Station to street & Oasis 21

EV.4 is the concourse-level change up toward Oasis 21. To reach street level itself, the building ground lifts are the step-free route: G1 (Sunshine Sakae), G2 (Oasis 21), G3 (Chunichi Building), G4 (Media Hiroba) and G5 (The Landmark Nagoya Sakae) — each pairs a spot on the concourse with a specific building’s own lift, not a subway elevator. Published hours: Oasis 21 6am–11pm, Chunichi Building 5:15am–midnight, Media Hiroba 5:30am–11:30pm, The Landmark 5:30am–midnight.

Hisaya-odori Station to street

The primary step-free route is EV.7, from the North Gate’s public side up to street level. Two more building lifts also reach the surface on timed access: C (Central Park) and U (Urban Net Nagoya Building). West Gate is not reachable by elevator from either line’s platforms — it depends on stairs.

Sourced from Nagoya City Transportation Bureau’s platform and gate accessibility guides for Hisaya-odori Station. We haven’t independently timed or photographed these routes yet.

Into Central Park

Central Park connects to Hisaya-odori Station’s North Gate area by lift C, on timed access, near the mall’s northern parking-access side. Inside, toilets are at four points; only the one near Exit 6B is marked as an accessible toilet on the mall’s own map, with a women’s toilet alongside it. Public passages are open 7am–10:30pm — shop and parking hours differ.

Sourced from Central Park’s official floor map and FAQ. Which floors lift C actually reaches, and whether a fully step-free route exists end to end, aren’t confirmed by that map — we haven’t independently checked this route yet.

Buses

Oasis 21 Bus Terminal (bays 1–10) and the separate Sakae City Bus Stops (west-side bays 18–20 plus nearby street stops) are both mapped below, under Floor plan.

Toilets 03

Toilets

Types4

Station

Sakae Station’s accessible toilet is outside the East Gate on B1, with an ostomate fitting. Hisaya-odori Station has three more: two inside the North Gate (approached via a ramp) and one outside the West Gate. All are marked in pink on the floor plan below.

Bus terminal

Oasis 21 Bus Terminal has two accessible toilets on the boarding level — one near the north entrance/ramp, one near the south entrance — both marked on the Oasis 21 map below.

Public toilets outside

Sakae Funsui-nishi Public Toilet (栄噴水西公衆トイレ), in Nishiki 3-chome, is the closest independent public toilet — about 54m from the station.

Wheelchair access for this specific toilet is not confirmed in the city’s public-toilet open data. If step-free access matters, the station or Oasis 21 toilets above are the safer bet.

Other: nearby large facilities

Matsuzakaya Nagoya, Mitsukoshi Nagoya Sakae, Sunshine Sakae, the Chunichi Building and The Landmark Nagoya Sakae are all a short walk from the station and open customer toilets during business hours. Japanese department stores typically keep a multi-purpose toilet on at least one floor, though the exact floor varies by store.
